Two valid integration points exist: (1) inside _parse_slot, replacing `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]` as the fallback before per-class overrides are applied; (2) inside load_class_slots or parse_class_slots, pre-populating the table before _parse_slot runs. findings.finding: Five existing test files that directly monkeypatch.setenv('REBAR_LLM_MODEL', ...) and then call into from_env() or load_class_slots() are unenumerated consumers: tests/unit/test_config_llm.py (lines 124, 182), tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py (line 114), tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py (line 454), tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py (lines 359–360), and tests/external/test_workflow_live.py (line 35). After this ticket lands, every such test will trigger warn_deprecated on a real env-read path. The plan's 'warn-when-set' semantic (check os.environ.get('REBAR_LLM_MODEL') is not None) means warnings fire in these tests even though their intent is to test existing precedence behavior, not the deprecation. Tests that use caplog or recwarn may receive unexpected records; at minimum the warning flood may obscure CI output. None of these test files are named in Scope or in Testing as consumers requiring cleanup or suppression.
findings.location: Scope / Testing sections; tests/unit/test_config_llm.py:124,182, tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:114, tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:454, tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py:359-360, tests/external/test_workflow_live.py:35

findings.finding: AC3 mandates that the four rendered operator-visible strings (`_cli/_llm_commands.py:160` `--help` text, `_mcp_llm.py:64` MCP tool description, `llm/config.py:10` module docstring, `llm/config.py:195` `resolve_model` docstring) must no longer present `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the current interface — but the criterion specifies only *removal*, not *replacement*. An operator who reads the deprecation warning during a run and then consults `--help` or an MCP client for the replacement knob would find a gap: the rendered surface has had the old reference stripped but gives no forward pointer to `REBAR_LLM_CLASS_MODEL` / `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]`. The prose-docs AC (the final AC) does require presenting the class configuration as the replacement, but it explicitly scopes itself to six `.md` files and carves out the rendered strings as 'a separate class with their own criterion' — that separate criterion (AC3) then says only 'no longer present … as the current interface', with no mention of a replacement pointer. The non-happy-path gap is: an operator mid-migration who has already acted on the deprecation warning has no in-process guidance on what to set instead.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC3 ('the four RENDERED references named in Scope no longer present `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the current model-selection interface')
scenarios: CLI shape: an operator running `rebar review --help` after seeing the deprecation warning sees that `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is no longer mentioned but finds no replacement knob documented in the help text, leaving them unable to complete migration without consulting external docs.

MCP shape: an MCP client surfacing the updated tool description sees the old env-var reference removed but receives no pointer to the replacement class-slot interface, breaking discovery for operators who rely on tool descriptions for configuration guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC3 to: 'each of the four rendered strings must both (a) no longer present `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the current interface AND (b) name or link to the replacement (`REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` / `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]`) so an operator reading `--help` or an MCP tool description during migration can find the new knob without leaving the tool.'
